correctness.rationale: The theorem uses the actual flat implication clause: x forces A ↝ B iff for every y≥x, the entire R[y] row is contained in A only when it is contained in B; this is not the pointwise R[x]∩A⊂B modality. Upward normalization replaces rows by U_y=↑R[y]. Every nonempty join-prime upset in a finite preorder equals a principal ↑z. Under PR, a future witness t to failure of (p∨q)↝r admits a contained principal row U_y=↑z with z≤t, hence this row lies in one antecedent and forces r, contradiction. If PR fails, select a minimal future row containing t within U_x; decompose the nonprincipal upset into proper upsets A∪B and use C=W\downarrow t to obtain both antecedent implications but false disjunctive implication. The 3-world fork is a sharp separation from pointwise downward directedness. Matrix search is O(|W|^4). Independent complete upset-valuation check on the specified 3-world example tested 375 valuations/world combinations, and the actual source checker algorithm was inspected; finite tests are not the all-finite proof.
